items.followUp: State two functions of the stem and two functions of the root.

rubric.why: The root system absorbs water and mineral salts from the soil and anchors the plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct root function, such as absorption of water and minerals or anchorage.

rubric.why: The shoot system bears leaves and other aerial parts; it supports the plant and carries out functions such as photosynthesis and transport.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct shoot function.

modelAnswer: The root system anchors the plant in the soil and absorbs water and mineral salts.
The shoot system bears the aerial parts, supports the plant, and carries out functions such as photosynthesis and transport.

items.followUp: Draw Fischer projections of glucose and fructose.

rubric.why: D-ribose is a five-carbon sugar with its hydroxyl groups on the right at C2, C3 and C4 in the Fischer projection.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct Fischer projection of D-ribose.

rubric.why: 2-deoxy-D-ribose is a common pentose; it has no hydroxyl group at C2 and has hydroxyl groups on the right at C3 and C4 in the Fischer projection.
rubric.description: Structure of the second common pentose
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct Fischer projection of 2-deoxy-D-ribose.

modelAnswer: Draw a Fischer projection of D-ribose with CHO at the top and CH2OH at the bottom.
At C2, C3 and C4 of D-ribose, place H on the left and OH on the right.
Draw a Fischer projection of 2-deoxy-D-ribose with CHO at the top and CH2OH at the bottom.
At C2 of 2-deoxy-D-ribose, place H on both sides; at C3 and C4, place H on the left and OH on the right.

items.followUp: What is the role of cellulose in the human diet?

rubric.why: Dietary fibre, or roughage, consists mainly of indigestible plant material such as cellulose.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying fibre as indigestible plant material or roughage.

rubric.why: Fibre adds bulk to faeces and helps bowel movement, reducing constipation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct benefit, such as promoting peristalsis or preventing constipation.

modelAnswer: Dietary fibre (roughage) is the indigestible part of plant food, mainly cellulose.
It adds bulk to faeces and promotes bowel movement, helping to prevent constipation.

items.followUp: Explain what happens to the two male gametes during fertilization in a flowering plant.

rubric.why: One male gamete fuses with the egg cell to form a diploid zygote.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying fusion of one male gamete with the egg to form a zygote.

rubric.why: The other male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei (or secondary nucleus) to form the endosperm; the two fusions together are double fertilization.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the second fusion and formation of endosperm.

modelAnswer: Double fertilization is the occurrence of two fusion events in the embryo sac of a flowering plant.
One male gamete fuses with the egg to form a zygote, while the other fuses with the two polar nuclei to form the endosperm.

items.followUp: Compare a rhizome with a tuber.

rubric.why: A bulb has a short stem with fleshy scale leaves that store food; onion is an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct distinguishing feature or example of a bulb.

rubric.why: A corm is a solid, swollen underground stem, usually covered by dry scale leaves; gladiolus and colocasia are examples.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct distinguishing feature or example of a corm.

modelAnswer: A bulb has a short stem surrounded by fleshy scale leaves that store food; onion is an example.
A corm is a solid, swollen underground stem covered with dry scale leaves; gladiolus is an example.

items.followUp: Describe the effect of temperature on enzyme activity and give an example.

rubric.why: Enzymes have an optimum pH; a change in pH can alter the active site, and extreme pH can denature the enzyme.
rubric.description: Effect of pH on enzyme activity
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining optimum pH or the effect of unsuitable pH on enzyme activity.

rubric.why: Pepsin works best in the acidic conditions of the stomach, while trypsin works best in an alkaline environment.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct enzyme and its suitable pH condition.

modelAnswer: Each enzyme has an optimum pH at which it works fastest; a change in pH alters its activity, and extreme pH may denature it.
For example, pepsin works best in acidic conditions, whereas trypsin works best in alkaline conditions.

items.followUp: Write the word equation for aerobic respiration and state one activity that requires its energy.

rubric.why: Cellular respiration is the breakdown or oxidation of food in cells, releasing energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining respiration as the cellular breakdown or oxidation of food that releases energy.

rubric.why: The released energy powers the activities of the organism, including metabolic processes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that respiration supplies energy for life or metabolic activities.

modelAnswer: Cellular respiration is the breakdown or oxidation of food, especially glucose, in cells to release energy.
This energy is used to carry out life activities and metabolic processes.

items.followUp: Write the equation for aerobic respiration and name the gas required for it.

rubric.why: Yeast forms ethanol (ethyl alcohol) by fermenting glucose in the absence of oxygen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing yeast fermentation of glucose under anaerobic conditions to form alcohol.

rubric.why: The fermentation equation shows glucose producing ethanol and carbon dioxide.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct balanced equation or equivalent word equation.

modelAnswer: In the absence of oxygen, yeast ferments glucose to form ethanol (ethyl alcohol) and carbon dioxide.
